neighbours.label: preposition/verb completing a participial or 'with'-phrase before its object ('looming over', 'presented ... by', 'in order to protect')
fire: With the threat of attacks looming over the city, the guards doubled.
Presented with a list of questions by email, the spokesperson declined.
In order to protect her children, she moved abroad.
In danger of losing its influence in the region, the empire struck first.
With an early 14-0 lead and a storm on their side, they won easily.
Instead of presenting a few candidates to the manager, he sent fifty.
With storms hanging over the coast, the ferry stayed in port.
Faced with a choice by the committee, she resigned.
quiet: The guards doubled because attacks were likely in the city.
The spokesperson declined to answer the questions.
She moved abroad with her children.
The empire struck first in the region.
They won easily in the storm.
He sent fifty candidates to the manager.
The ferry stayed in port on the coast.
